IC_considered_not_counted: section 2 item 8 (compliance metric computed from a repair=False parse) vs item 2 (cluster_cmd passes repair=True): A does not say where first-parse state is carried; an omission, not a stated opposite.
section 2 item 6 ('--resume ... documented nowhere') vs section 3.3 (E2 spike S2 passed --resume): documented vs tested, not opposed.

IC_contradiction_list.side1: section 1: "It touches no field the limits do not name."
IC_contradiction_list.side2: section 5 'Reference tokens survive the cut': "The step therefore copies any reference token found only in the cut text into `refs` while it has room (cap 8), and records `refs_lost` otherwise." (A itself adds: "it is not in E2 R-02")
IC_contradiction_list.why: The step writes to `refs`, which is not one of the fields the limits name (anchor, anchor2, quote, claim).

IC_contradiction_list.side1: line 5: "Truncate `anchor` and `anchor2` to 200 and `claim` to 300 as an exact prefix"
IC_contradiction_list.side2: section 2 item 7: "claim to 297 characters plus `...` ... Position A takes that exact rule as the claim cut"
IC_contradiction_list.why: A claim of 297 characters plus a marker is not an exact prefix of the first 300 characters; A's own item 7 says only anchors, anchor2 and quote are cut as exact prefixes.

IC_contradiction_list.side1: section 1: "removes 88 of the 92 measured drops, so ... the expensive, unmeasured step (re-ask) is left with at most 4 lines" (and section 3.4 "at most 4 lines")
IC_contradiction_list.side2: section 3.1: "88 of 92 ... [derived upper bound, not measured]" and section 5 M1: "a lower number means a second violation on the same line"
IC_contradiction_list.why: An upper bound on lines the cut can fix is a lower bound on the residual (at least 4); "at most 4" cannot follow from it, and A's own M1 allows a larger residual.

IC_considered_not_counted: section 3.2 (re-ask only for blocking true/unknown drops) vs section 2 C-02 row (any over-limit line makes block_ok False until the re-ask): a reviewer whose only drops say blocking:false never regains a valid block; an unaddressed gap, not a stated opposite.

section 4.5 bullet 4 (SKILL.md:343 forbids any normalisation by the orchestrator) vs last bullet (a code normaliser bears on where a repair may live): B qualifies itself in the same list; not opposed.

IC_contradiction_list.side1: section 4.4 totals and 4.6: "all 5 re-asked blocks recorded valid afterwards" / "5 of 5 re-asked blocks recorded valid"
IC_contradiction_list.side2: section 4.4 table, row E3: "reviewer 3 fully fixed; reviewer 2 still had two bad citations; '3 of 3 (to be confirmed by `review cluster`)'"
IC_contradiction_list.why: B's own table shows a re-asked block that was still invalid and one outcome unconfirmed, so "5 of 5 valid" is not supported by the table beside it.

IC_contradiction_list.side1: section 4.2 'What this gives B': "and on none of the 42 merges where a blocking row survived"
IC_contradiction_list.side2: section 4.2 table: "49 rows in 44 distinct triples and 42 distinct (row, package) merges" and "4 rows in 3 merges" where no blocking row was left
IC_contradiction_list.why: The 42 merges are all merges with a dropped blocking line, 3 of which have no surviving blocking row; the merges where a blocking row survived number 39, not 42.

IC_contradiction_list.side1: sections 3.5 and 5 (INV-C, B-raise): "rewrites four boundary assertions"
IC_contradiction_list.side2: section 3.1 and section 2 INV-010 row: `card_convert.py` (`MAX_CLAIM = 300`) "must import the same constants under either policy"; its pin `tests/review/test_review_card_convert.py:500` asserts `len(f["claim"]) == 300`
IC_contradiction_list.why: If card_convert imports the raised claim constant, a fifth pin (test_review_card_convert.py:500, read at HEAD) fails; B's count of four omits it.
